Implement a module named fifo_8x8 — a synchronous first-in first-out buffer that
holds up to 8 entries of 8 bits each.

Interface:
  - input        clk
  - input        rst        (synchronous reset, active high)
  - input        wr_en
  - input        rd_en
  - input  [7:0] data_in
  - output [7:0] data_out
  - output       full
  - output       empty
  - output [3:0] count      (number of entries currently stored, 0 to 8)

Behaviour, all state changes on the rising edge of clk:

  Reset: when rst is high on a rising edge, the buffer becomes empty (count
  returns to 0) and data_out becomes 8'd0. Reset takes priority over wr_en and
  rd_en.

  Write: when wr_en is high and the buffer is not full, data_in is stored at the
  tail. A write while full is ignored and the stored data is unchanged.

  Read: when rd_en is high and the buffer is not empty, the entry at the head is
  removed and driven onto data_out. data_out is REGISTERED: it updates on the
  same rising edge that performs the read, so the value read is visible after
  that edge. A read while empty is ignored and data_out keeps its previous value.

  Simultaneous read and write in the same cycle is allowed whenever the write is
  permitted and the read is permitted; count is then unchanged.

Status outputs, all combinational functions of the current count:
  - empty is 1 when count is 0
  - full  is 1 when count is 8
  - count is the current number of stored entries

Entries are returned in the order they were written.

This is a sequential circuit.
